evals.name: answer-round-then-execute
evals.prompt: Split this and run it in the supplied disposable local test database: migrate the analytics events to a new schema whose name I have intentionally not supplied yet, then delete the old test tables once nothing reads them. Ask for the missing schema name before inspecting local files or running anything.
evals.followup: The new schema is analytics_v2. The disposable database is ./analytics-test.sqlite and its query log is ./fixture-query.log. Use a full code-reference scan plus that fixture query log as the check; yes, drop the old test tables after that check, using only this disposable local database. Go ahead.
evals.expected_output: Turn one shows draft artifacts plus one questions block with recommended answers and stops; turn two echoes the updated artifacts, then executes on the go-ahead in the answer message.
expectations: Turn one: draft artifacts shown, one questions block with a recommended answer per question, no Go?, no execution despite run it
Turn one: no local-primer or repository reads; supplied/local test inputs do not imply prior joint work
Turn one: final status is ❓ Need you
Turn two: updated artifacts are shown again before anything runs
Turn two: the go-ahead in the answer message counts as run it and execution begins after the echo
Turn two: the shown artifacts are executed without being sharpened again
evals.setup: Before the first turn, run the supplied setup.py into an empty disposable directory. Use that directory as cwd. Supply only prompt first; send followup after the first result. The historical fixture uses analytics_v2 as the target table, as explained in its README. Never use a live database.
